html:
The war of 1990 and 1991 in which a coalition led by the United States drove Iraq out of Kuwait, which it had invaded and annexed.

Saddam Hussein came out of his long war with Iran deep in debt, much of it to Kuwait. He accused Kuwait of pumping too much oil and keeping prices low, and Iraq had long claimed it. On 2 August 1990 Iraqi troops overran the country. The United Nations imposed sanctions and set a deadline for withdrawal. Some 35 countries sent forces, which gathered in Saudi Arabia.

The air war began on 17 January 1991, shown live on television to the world. After five weeks of bombing, a ground attack on 24 February broke the Iraqi army in about a hundred hours. As they left, Iraqi troops set hundreds of oil wells alight (Kuwaiti oil fires), which burned for months.

Saddam stayed in power and crushed uprisings by Shia Arabs and Kurds in 1991. Iraq lived under harsh sanctions for over a decade. The war came just as the Cold War ended, with the Soviet Union standing aside. American troops stayed in Saudi Arabia, which became a grievance used by Osama bin Laden. The unfinished business ended in the American invasion of Iraq in 2003.
sum: The war of 1990 and 1991 in which a coalition led by the United States drove Iraq out of Kuwait, which it had invaded and annexed.
